label: Combined Fanonian psychopathology of race with Brazilian Black feminist critique
description: Drawing deeply on Fanon's Black Skin, White Masks, Lélia Gonzalez diagnosed Brazilian society's "racial democracy" ideology as a collective neurosis of disavowal that splits and racializes Black women.
dialecticalTension: Translates Fanonian colonial psychology into Afro-Brazilian and Amefrican intersectionality.
historicalContext: Unified Black Movement (MNU) and Brazilian critical theory (1978–1994).

citations.author: Lélia Gonzalez
citations.work: Racismo e sexismo na cultura brasileira

label: Adapted Lacanian psychoanalysis (infans/lalangue) to theorize Pretuguês
description: Applying Lacan's concepts of infans, denegation, and linguistic unconscious, Gonzalez formulated "Pretuguês" (Blackened Portuguese) to reveal how African mothers shaped the very unconscious tongue of Brazilian culture.
dialecticalTension: Subverts Eurocentric Lacanian psychoanalysis to center repressed Afro-diasporic speech.
historicalContext: Delivered at ANPOCS and published in Revista Ciências Sociais Hoje (1984).

citations.author: Lélia Gonzalez
citations.work: Racismo e sexismo na cultura brasileira

label: Coined Amefricanidade as transnational Afro-Indigenous political epistemology
description: Gonzalez invented Amefricanidade (1988) to replace Eurocentric "Latin America," uniting the historical consciousness of African and Indigenous survival across the entire hemisphere.
dialecticalTension: Reframes American modernity from the epistemic vantage of quilombos and palenques.

label: Mentored and pioneered Black feminist epistemology inherited by Sueli Carneiro
description: As intellectual pioneer of Brazil's Black women's movement, Gonzalez laid the conceptual foundation upon which Sueli Carneiro constructed her theory of the raciality apparatus and epistemicide.
dialecticalTension: Continuity from psychoanalytic-cultural Amefricanidade to Foucauldian anti-epistemicide philosophy.

citations.author: Sueli Carneiro
citations.work: Enegrecer o feminismo / Escritos de uma vida

label: Pioneered interlocking race-gender-class critique parallel to Black feminist standpoint
description: Working in the 1980s alongside and prior to Anglo-American formulations of intersectionality, Gonzalez's analysis of the Black woman's structural position in Brazil profoundly complements Patricia Hill Collins's matrix of domination.
dialecticalTension: Bridges North American Black Feminist Thought with South American Amefricanidade.
